maya: quick heads-up — ran a bitsandbytes weight-only INT8 pass on Zephyr-14B today against our longform summarization slice. big perf win (≈2.8x tokens/s) but a puzzling non-monotonic quality regression on ~5% of docs, not uniform across prompt types.

alex: can you paste the eval slice metrics? which seeds/prompts?

maya: pasted raw numbers below. slice = longform-news (avg len 1.2k tokens). baseline fp16 vs int8-w-only (b&b 0.39 + `--bnb-quantize-weightonly`).

maya: ```
baseline fp16: ROUGE-L 42.8, perplexity 12.1, latency 110ms/token
int8-wonly: ROUGE-L 40.9, perplexity 13.4, latency 39ms/token
delta: -1.9 ROUGE-L, +1.3 ppl, throughput +2.8x
failure subset ~5% of docs where output became repetitive / hallucinated facts
```

kevin: interesting. do we see a correlation with input length or specific tokens? any tokenizer mismatch?

maya: ran quick stratification: the regressions skew to docs with lots of numeric tables and long bullet lists. also higher for examples with many short quoted spans. tokenizer seems identical (same tokenizer hash).

rachel: did you try `llm.int8` vs bitsandbytes variant? sometimes weight-only implementations differ on per-head scaling.

maya: yes — tried both: `bitsandbytes` weight-only card + bnb v0.41 and our `llm.int8` path. both show the same subset failing, but magnitude slightly different (llm.int8 delta -1.6 ROUGE-L).

alex: can you dump a couple of example generations (fp16 vs int8) for inspection? short diffs only.

maya: posted two pairs to the eval bucket (links: https://internal/evals/zephyr/2054321000/1 and /2). quick excerpt: fp16 preserves table cells and numeric formatting; int8 collapses some cells into one paragraph and invents a number.

eval-bot: automated eval notes: ngram-heavy metrics show biggest drop; factuality classifier prob drops from 0.87 -> 0.61 on that subset.

kevin: sounds like per-head scaling noise causing token logit reshaping on fine-grained numeric tokens. can we try group-wise quantization (group size 128) or per-channel scaling if supported?

maya: plan: 1) re-run with group_size=128, 2) enable `use_fast_norm=True` fallback, 3) re-run with per-layer threshold clipping (0.01) on sensitive layers (attention output). queued jobs now: `python -m bench.run --model zephyr-14b --quant bnb --group 128 --clip 0.01 --slice longform-news`

rachel: also try a small post-processing mitigation: for outputs where confidence on numeric spans < 0.7, call the fp16 fallback route for that request. may be feasible in dedicated pool with routing policy.

alex: good pragmatic approach. what's the deploy risk if we ship this variant to Dedicated? 

maya: rollout proposal: canary 2% traffic on dedicated, monitor ROUGE-L and factuality for the longform slice, auto-roll back on regression >1.0 ROUGE-L or factuality drop >0.15. latency + cost gains are significant so we want it available, but only as an option with strict SLAs.

kevin: also instrument token-level logits diff histogram and KV cache anomaly flag. helps root-causing whether quantization noise accumulates through layers.

maya: will add traces to Redwood Console: per-token KL and a small eval-set checkpoint every 1h.

rachel: if group_size=128 fixes most failures with minor perf loss (say 2.2x instead of 2.8x), that sounds reasonable. otherwise consider hybrid: use int8 for tokens not in numeric spans, fp16 for numeric spans detected via quick regex.

maya: yup — that hybrid routing might be the lowest-risk path. I'll post updated numbers when the jobs finish (ETA ~30m). thanks all. :rocket:

alex: thanks — ping here when done.

maya: update 30m: group_size=128 reduced the failing subset to ~1.3% and ROUGE-L delta is now -0.6. throughput at 2.2x. job logs: `run-2054321000-gs128.log` in the bucket.

kevin: that's promising. let's run an adversarial prompt sweep focused on numeric/table fidelity and then propose rollout + fallback config.

maya: filing a tiny RFC for the canary config and eval gating (will link).
